components.name: Approval gate
components.description: Human-Gate or Agent-Gate. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.4. One kind, two modes; they differ only in who decides. reviewer: human parks the run as waiting_human. reviewer: agent is a machine check whose verdict is {pass, reason}; today that check is an LLM judge. mode: check is RESERVED and refused. A human gate is optional. Without a key the agent-gate does not wave anything through — it escalates to a human.

escalateOn.notes: objection hands a failed check to a person. Default objection.

status.notes: reviewer: human — the run is waiting_human until q-core approve continues it or --reject fails it.

components.name: llm-call/openrouter
components.description: OpenRouter inference with an explicit model, a local secret reference from the environment or the macOS Keychain, bounded retries and timeout, an optional per-call money cap, and the provider's own cost in the run record. This is not the current CLI agent.

input.notes: One step-output reference, for example {{steps.unique.output}}; the model then sees only that value instead of every prior output (capped at 60 000 characters). A reference that does not resolve fails before anything is sent.

secretSource.notes: env | keychain. Default env. keychain reads the key from the local macOS Keychain (service com.qfactory.q-core.openrouter, account openrouter:<keyRef>; store it with q-core auth set openrouter); the key never appears in the workflow, environment or run record.

keyRef.notes: Uppercase secret alias, default OPENROUTER_API_KEY. With secretSource env it names the environment variable; with keychain it names the Keychain entry.

retries.notes: 0..5, default 2. At most retries + 1 billable attempts; retried only on network, timeout, 429 and 5xx. Out of range fails the step before the key is read.

maxCallCostUsd.notes: Optional per-call money cap in USD, (0, 100]. The worst case of every attempt at the model's listed price must fit, or the call is not made (COST_LIMIT); a model with no listed price is refused (COST_UNKNOWN).

json.notes: When format: json, the output is the parsed object instead of {text, model}.

costUsd.notes: Run record: costUsd is the provider's reported cost (costSource provider), else the listed price of the model that answered (rate-table), else null (unknown). A finite budgetUsd stops the next paid step while any cost is unknown.

components.name: Telegram publish
components.description: A named recipe over api-request, not a new engine kind. POSTs to Telegram sendMessage with {{env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}} and {{env.TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}}. The runner still executes api-request (SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.3). Unset env vars do not fire a URL with braces in it — the runner writes to .qf/out/ and says so (SPEC §9).

text.notes: Message body. In shipped workflows this is a prior step's output, templated into api-request body.

sent.notes: Recipe surface, not an engine field. True when the api-request completed; false when the file sink was used instead.

chatId.notes: Optional. The chat that was addressed. Not an engine field — the request body carries chat_id.

core.source: Core.35 successor of Core.34: only a person decides a human gate. q-core approve (and --reject) prints the subject and a one-time code on the controlling terminal (/dev/tty, never stdout) and continues only when the code is typed back there; it refuses inside an agent session (CLAUDECODE, AI_AGENT, CODEX_SANDBOX and similar markers), without a terminal or with piped input, exits 2 and leaves the run waiting; q-core run --json returns nextAction ask_human_to_approve for a parked run; the library resumeRun requires a confirmation record. Same manifest validator, YAML parser and request schema; SPEC-MANIFEST documents the human gate
core.acceptanceRecord: Owner acceptance is recorded outside the immutable release, at acceptance/<releaseVersion>.json in the Registry root
